questions.question: A sum amounts to ₹7,500 in 2 years and ₹8,250 in 3 years at simple interest. The sum is
questions.explanation: One year's interest = 8250 − 7500 = ₹750. Interest for 2 years = ₹1,500. Principal = 7500 − 1500 = ₹6,000.

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself in 20 years at simple interest. The rate per annum is
questions.explanation: Tripling means SI = 2P. 2P = P × R × 20 / 100, so R = 200/20 = 10%.

questions.question: ₹2,550 is divided into two parts so that the simple interest on one part at 6% for 3 years equals that on the other at 8% for 2 years. The larger part is
questions.explanation: Let the parts be x and y. 6 × 3 × x = 8 × 2 × y, so 18x = 16y and x : y = 8 : 9. Total parts = 17, one part = 150. Larger part = 9 × 150 = ₹1,350.

A sum of money triples itself in 12 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become 5 times itself?
questions.explanation: Tripling needs interest 2P in 12 years, so 6 years earn P. Five times needs interest 4P, which takes 4 × 6 = 24 years.
questions.shortcut: Each extra "P" of interest takes the same time.
